info.title: bloomin API
info.description:
API of bloomin: one bingo card shared by everyone who joins it.

## Signing requests

There is no login. A device makes an Ed25519 key pair and a participant id (lowercase UUID), keeps the private key in the keychain (synced with iCloud Keychain), and registers the public key with `POST /v1/participants`. Every request, registration included, carries three headers:

- `Bloomin-Participant-Id`: the participant id.
- `Bloomin-Timestamp`: Unix time in whole seconds, decimal.
- `Bloomin-Signature`: the Ed25519 signature of the signing string below, standard base64 with padding.

The signing string is these five lines joined by a single `\n` (LF), with no line break at the end, encoded as UTF-8:

```
bloomin-v1
<METHOD>
<path and query>
<timestamp>
<body SHA-256>
```

- `METHOD`: the HTTP method exactly as sent; every method of this API is uppercase.
- `path and query`: the request path exactly as sent, percent-encoding as on the wire, followed by `?` and the query when the URL has one. No scheme, host or fragment.
- `timestamp`: the same text as the `Bloomin-Timestamp` header.
- `body SHA-256`: SHA-256 of the raw body bytes, 64 lowercase hex digits. A request without a body hashes zero bytes (`e3b0c442…b855`).

The signature is accepted only in its one canonical base64 encoding. The server refuses with 401 when the timestamp is more than 300 seconds from its clock, or when the signature does not verify with the participant's registered key (for registration, the key in the body, and the participant id header must equal the body `id`). A request that changes something (any method but GET) is accepted once: the server remembers its signature until the timestamp leaves the window and refuses the same signature again with 401. A GET may be sent again. To retry a change, sign it again with a new timestamp. Requests that create something (a card, a note, a photo) carry an id the app makes, so a retry returns what the first request made instead of making it twice. Worked examples are in `server/test-vectors/signature.json`.

## Deadline

A card stores its last day and the creator's IANA time zone. It expires at 00:00 of the following day in that zone. After that it is read-only, except that photos can still be added and people can still join to look at it.

## Stamping

Items are never stamped by picking them from the card. The app sends a one-line note, with a `noteId` it makes, to `POST /v1/cards/{cardId}/stamps` and the server stamps the items the note fulfils, which may be none or several.

## Errors

Every error body is `ErrorBody`, including 404 for a path no route has. A body that is not JSON where JSON is expected, or JSON that does not match the schema, gets 400 `invalid_request`.

## Joining

The QR code holds the Universal Link `https://<host>/j/{joinCode}`. The app reads the code from the link and calls `POST /v1/joins`.

Size.description: The card is size × size. Odd sizes have a FREE cell in the middle.

date.description: Last day of the card, in the creator's time zone.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone name of the creator. Letter case is not significant; responses carry the spelling the server's time zone data resolves it to (`asia/tokyo` comes back as `Asia/Tokyo`).

Deadline.description: The card expires at the first instant on or after 00:00 of the day after `date`, in `timeZone`. The server decides this on every request.

Card.description: Every member sees the same card and the same layout.

JoinCode.description: 10 characters of Crockford base32 (uppercase). The QR holds the Universal Link https://<host>/j/{joinCode}. Rotating the code makes old QR codes stop working.

Item.description: One cell. The FREE cell has no item.

Position.description: Cell index, row-major from the top left: 0 … size²−1.

ItemTitle.description: One line without control, private-use, unassigned, direction-override or tag characters, with at least one visible letter, digit, punctuation or symbol; length is counted in Unicode code points after trimming.

Emoji.description: One emoji: a single extended grapheme cluster holding an emoji.

stampedAt.description: Instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with Z.

Stamp.description: At most one per item. Made from a one-line note, never by picking an item. Editing the item keeps the stamp; any member can remove it.

NoteId.description: Made by the app for each note it sends, so a retry can be told from a new note.

Comment.description: The one-line note of what was done. One line without control, private-use, unassigned, direction-override or tag characters, with at least one visible letter, digit, punctuation or symbol; length is counted in Unicode code points after trimming.

achievedAt.description: Instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with Z.

Bingo.description: A completed line, kept as the items it held (FREE left out) and the time. It does not change when items, positions or the size change later.

BingoItem.description: The item as it was when the bingo was made.

takenAt.description: Instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with Z.

uploadedAt.description: Instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with Z.

Photo.description: The image itself is read from GET /v1/cards/{cardId}/photos/{photoId}.

joinedAt.description: Instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with Z.

allOf.description: Made by the app, so a retry returns the card the first request made.

items.description: One item for every position except the FREE cell.
Every item of the resized card. Existing items left out are deleted with their stamps. The server places the items at random.

allOf.description: An existing item to keep, with its stamp. Omit for a new item.

stamps.description: The stamps this note made: none when it fulfils no unstamped item, several when it fulfils several.

post.description: No login. Signed like every other request, with two differences: the `Bloomin-Participant-Id` header must equal the `id` in the body, and the signature is checked with the public key in the body, so the participant need not exist yet. Registering again with the same id and key returns the existing participant.

post.summary: Stamp the items a one-line note fulfils
post.description: Items are never stamped by picking them. The server judges from the note which unstamped items it fulfils (none, one or several), stamps each with who sent the note, the note and the time, then records any bingo they completed. An item already stamped keeps its stamp: when two notes fulfil one item, the first one to arrive stamps it. The same sender sending the same `noteId` again returns the stamps that note made, with no new bingos, without judging it again.

put.summary: Add a photo to a bingo
put.description: Allowed after the deadline. The body is the image bytes, at most 10485760 bytes; its SHA-256 is part of the signature like any body. Another content type or an empty body gets 400 `invalid_request`. The app makes `photoId`; sending the same one again returns the photo the first request stored.
